params.body:
Closes #997
Closes #998

Replaces #1000, which went red on "Changed PHP is formatted" over the spacing in its new test file (pint's `concat_space` and `binary_operator_spaces`). Same change, rebased on main of today, the test file formatted by pint, the targeted tests and the full suite run again. #1000 can be closed.

A dealer wanted to stop the daily bidding digest. He clicked "Beheer je voorkeuren" in the mail and got the 403 page (Portal mail 15, 12 October 2026). Had he reached the field, it could not have given him what he asked.

## Why

- `mails/export_daily_mail.blade.php` built the footer link as `route('dealer.edit', $dealer_id)`: the administrator's garage sheet, behind the `dealers` menu right, so the Access middleware sends a dealer to 403. (It also passed the raw id where the route reads a base64 one.)
- The field "Mail samenvatting biedingswagens per dag" (`dealers.mail_once_per_day`) was yes or no: `1` the daily digest (`DailyExports`), `0` a mail at every new or changed bidding (`MailHelper::sendMails`). There was no "none". The only way to silence the mails was to take module 2 away, which also takes the biddings away.

## What changes

- The footer link opens the reader's own garage sheet (`ownuser.edit`, base64 id), which every user of that garage may open (R P2-1.11) and which carries the field. A merchant has no login, so his daily mail (there is none since 21 September) would carry no link.
- The field becomes "Mails over nieuwe biedingen" with three choices in the same column: at every new bidding (`0`), one digest per day (`1`), none (`2`), as `Dealer::BIDDING_MAILS_EACH|DAILY|NONE` with `Dealer::biddingMailOptions()` for the select, in nl, fr, en and de. The daily task selects `DAILY` only and the creation and change mails go to `EACH` only, both written against the constants now. "None" keeps the dealer in module 2 and in the mails about the biddings he took part in (ended, won, lost), which never read this flag. `DealerRequest` refuses any other value.
- Rules R B1-1.11 and R B1-2.4 name the third choice and where the footer link leads.
- `BiddingMailPreferencesTest`: a "none" dealer gets neither the creation mail nor the digest while a "daily" and an "each" dealer get theirs, and stays in module 2; the footer link of the daily mail is the own garage sheet and not the administrator's, and a user of that garage opens it with a 200 and sees the choice "geen"; the choice is saved from the own sheet and an unknown value is refused.

No migration: the column keeps its name and type (tinyint); existing values `0` and `1` keep their meaning.

## Checks

- `BiddingMailPreferencesTest`, `BiddingMailsTest`, `EveryMailFollowsTheHouseRulesTest`, `LanguageParityTest`, `DealerAuthorizationTest`, `GarageAdministrationIsForAdministratorsTest`, `AMerchantBidsOnlyInHisOwnGarageTest`, `BiddingTypeChoiceTest`, `RulesCoverageTest`, `RulesIdentityTest`: green.
- PHPStan: no errors.
- Pint on the new test file: green.
- Full suite on the workbench: 3048 tests, all green except the six cases of `APhotoWithoutAForegroundIsNotAFaultTest`, which fail identically on the other branch of this mail (a `Log::warning` count in the photo-answer flow, which this change does not touch; known to fail on a reused local test database).

## After the merge

The dealer who asked can set "geen" himself from the mail's footer link or on his garage sheet (tab 1, under the bidding module). Stocklist-beheer can also set it on his garage sheet.
params.title: A dealer can choose no mail about new biddings, and the mail's footer leads him there
